title: Canopy Tide
context: I wanted to prove that bespoke, scroll-driven build work could hold its own against agency-level real estate sites, without the agency price tag or timeline.
mandate: So I built Canopy & Tide myself: a fictional Bali villa, Casa del Sol, told across seven full-screen scenes with a scroll-driven 3D camera move, a custom water shader on the pool, and drifting particle detail, in under 48 hours.
result: It's become the reference piece for the studio's top end: the thing that makes "the site becomes the brand" land in a single scroll rather than a sentence.

title: Miller Hudson
context: Miller Hudson ran a serviced-accommodation coaching programme for property investors and landlords, but their cold traffic had nowhere clean to land, no page built to turn a click into an application.
mandate: They asked me to design and build a single VSL funnel page: video sales letter structure, anchor navigation, a countdown block and a Typeform application flow, refined across several rounds of client and mentor feedback.
result: The finished funnel now routes applications straight into their existing intake process, and it opened the door to a bigger conversation: a Meta Pixel and an ongoing retainer.

title: Retyred
context: Re-Tyred needed more than a website, they needed the whole thing done properly: brand, build and a clean professional handover, not just a link at the end.
mandate: I ran the entire engagement myself: brand and build, a live deployment, a proper agreement to stay on and help make sure their site went from bad to good.
result: Retyred is live at retyred.co.uk, and it's the studio's reference for how the whole process should feel to a client, brief to keys handed over.

title: Crown Civil Engineering
context: Crown Civil Engineering had no brand and no site, a civil engineering firm competing in an industry where almost everyone looks the same: stock photos, generic templates, nothing to remember them by.
mandate: They asked me to build both from nothing: a full identity (a cream, navy and red palette, a bespoke digger-arm mark taken through several iterations) and a website coded on Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind and Framer Motion.
result: CCE went from having nothing to owning a complete visual system and a live-ready site, proof a client can start with a blank page and leave with a brand.

title: Garage Rooms
context: Garage Rooms sell garden and garage rooms across a growing catalogue, and needed a site that could scale with new rooms and specs without turning into a mess of one-off pages.
mandate: I'm building them a Next.js 15 App Router site around a spec-card design system: dynamic room detail pages, a working finance calculator and a booking flow wired through an API route.
result: Still in build, but it's already doing real work rather than just looking the part, a genuine application behind the brochure front, ready to grow as the catalogue does.

title: The Conservatory
context: The Conservatory is a plant shop and café in Hove that wanted a site with the same care as the space itself, not a generic hospitality template.
mandate: I ran a full creative direction session and moodboard, then spec'd and I'm now building the stack: Next.js on the front, Supabase for data (region-set to London) and Resend for transactional emails.
result: Still in progress, but the architecture is already doing the job: a small hospitality business getting a real backend, not just a nice-looking page.
